summary: Round-3 test pass of the diagram/sketch work in index.html (ports and pins, free mind maps, sequence diagrams, SVG/PNG download, freehand sketches). I wrote 143 Playwright tests under tests/01-for-index-html-page-please-add/ (model.spec.js, modal.spec.js, sketch.spec.js, extra.spec.js; run with `npx playwright test` from the repo root, PW_CHROME_PATH=/usr/bin/google-chrome-stable if the bundled browser is missing). 141 pass and 2 fail, and both failures are the same bug. Covered and passing: the flow `.port` text format and round-trips; dgPorts/dgAutoPort against the spec table and the real SVG outlines; self-edges; the mind-map `{x,y #color from= to=}` attributes, layout, own colours, whole-branch drag as one undo step, Auto layout, new-node placement, end handles and pinning; the sequence grammar, layout formulas, numbering, reorder by drag, label edit (Enter/Shift+Enter/Esc/blur), unicode ids and keyword ids; SVG/PNG export (white rect first, well-formed XML, 2x PNG, no modal markup), file names and per-kind numbering from preview and modal buttons; the coloured-edge CSS fix in preview and in the exported page; the sketch modal (pen, highlighter, eraser, 6 colours, 3 sizes, undo/redo keys, second-pointer cancel, pen/touch pointers, cancel confirm, Insert numbering and padding, one markdown undo step); the hover pencil on pictures and picture replacement (duplicates, big/small pictures, moved/deleted token, unloadable picture toast); i18n keys in both languages; XSS escaping; regex-backtracking and 400-message/60-participant robustness. Only one defect found (bug-1, low). Not covered: real touch gestures, a real cross-origin image without CORS headers (Playwright's route.fulfill bypasses CORS, so the tainted-canvas refusal could not be reproduced), and `/verify` nav-sync and the pre-existing tests/*.js suites. The implementer's report says tests/diagram.js and tests/sketch.js were not written and `/apptest diagram` was not run; tests/diagram.js does not exist in the repo. Test-harness notes: tests/01-*/debug.tmp.js and a stray docs/tasks/01-*/package.json (created by an `npm init -y` run from the wrong folder, which I could not delete because rm is refused) are left uncommitted; delete them.

bugs.description: The ◇ Diagram modal and the ✏ Sketch modal can be open at the same time. Focus is not trapped in either modal, so Tab walks out of the modal onto the page toolbar behind it, and pressing Enter on the ✏ Sketch button (while the diagram modal is open) or the ◇ Diagram button (while the sketch modal is open) opens the second full-screen modal on top of the first. `openDiagram()` guards only against itself (`if (dg.open) return`) and `openSketch()` guards only against itself (`if (sk.open) return`); neither checks the other modal. The two modals then share the keyboard (Esc, Ctrl+Z, P/H/E keys go to whichever handler sees them) and the lower one keeps unsaved state.
bugs.repro_steps: 1. Open index.html. 2. Click ◇ Diagram in the toolbar (the modal opens). 3. Press Tab repeatedly until the ✏ Sketch toolbar button has focus (about 20-30 presses; it is reachable). 4. Press Enter. 5. In the console check `[dg.open, sk.open]`. Reverse order: click ✏ Sketch, Tab to ◇ Diagram, Enter -> same result. Automated: tests/01-for-index-html-page-please-add/extra.spec.js, 'the sketch and diagram modals cannot both be opened at once from the toolbar' and 'and the other way round'.
bugs.expected: Only one of the two modals is ever open: the second open call is ignored (or the first modal is closed/confirmed first), and focus stays inside the open modal.
bugs.actual: `[dg.open, sk.open]` is `[true, true]`: both modals are visible and active at once.
